nodes.label: n002
nodes.author: 0b3c69814f295bb73e4affb25fd2d88a5765e598b047809149edb8954041e584
nodes.hypothesis: Giving the model the full symbol signatures and one worked example of the reply shape raises the pass rate, because most failures are wrong shape, not wrong logic.
nodes.statusReason: 2 verifications from distinct keys, every one at or above +1000bp. Worst delta +7000bp. This is a real improvement. The ledger is a local log, so one person can hold every key. Distinct keys are not proof of distinct people. Run `petri topic create` to publish.

proposal.hypothesis: Giving the model the full symbol signatures and one worked example of the reply shape raises the pass rate, because most failures are wrong shape, not wrong logic.
proposal.falsifiedIf: The candidate median score is not at least 1000 basis points above the parent median.
proposal.reasoning: The baseline prompt names the symbols but never shows their signatures or the reply shape. A model that guesses the shape fails a correct algorithm. Showing both removes that whole failure class.

nodes.diff:
--- a/harness/prompt.ts
+++ b/harness/prompt.ts
@@ -1,20 +1,23 @@
 /**
  * LEVER: `prompt` — what the harness says to the model.
  *
- * V1 is the honest baseline, and it carries a real defect on purpose.
- * `buildUserPrompt` sends the exported symbol NAMES only. It never sends the
- * full signatures, so the model has to guess the argument order and the argument
- * types. That headroom is deliberate. It is the first thing a reader should see.
+ * V2 closes the two gaps V1 left open on purpose.
  *
+ *   - `buildUserPrompt` sends the FULL SIGNATURE of every exported symbol, not
+ *     the bare name. The model no longer guesses the argument order, the
+ *     argument types or the return shape. (motif: include-signatures)
+ *   - `buildSystemPrompt` carries ONE worked example of the reply shape. The
+ *     model no longer guesses the output format. (motif: one-worked-example)
+ *
+ * Both lines are paid for on every call of every task, so the example is kept to
+ * four lines. The measured trade-off is more input tokens for a higher score.
+ *
  * Things a later node might try here:
- *   - send `s.signature` as well as `s.name` (motif: include-signatures)
- *   - add one worked example of the exact reply shape (motif: one-worked-example)
  *   - state the output format as a hard rule instead of a sentence
  *   - name the file extension and the module system in the system text
  *   - reorder the parts, so the task text is last and stays closest to the answer
- *
- * Keep the system text short. It is sent on every call of every task, so each
- * added line is paid for 20 times per run and 100 times per 5-run median.
+ *   - drop the worked example again and keep only the signatures, to find out
+ *     which of the two changes carried the win
  */
 import type { TaskView } from './contract.js';
 import type { RetrievedContext } from './retrieval.js';
@@ -24,6 +27,13 @@
     'You are a JavaScript programmer.',
     'Write complete, runnable ESM code.',
     'Reply with one fenced code block and nothing else.',
+    'Reply in exactly this shape:',
+    '```js',
+    'export function example(input, size) {',
+    "  if (!Array.isArray(input)) throw new TypeError('input must be an array');",
+    '  return [];',
+    '}',
+    '```',
   ].join('\n');
 }
 
@@ -31,8 +41,11 @@
   const parts: string[] = [];
   parts.push(`Task: ${task.prompt}`);
   parts.push(`Write the file ${task.entryFile}.`);
-  // V1 sends symbol NAMES only. The full signatures are deliberately withheld.
-  parts.push(`It must export: ${task.exportedSymbols.map((s) => s.name).join(', ')}.`);
+  // V2 sends the FULL signature of every symbol. V1 sent the names only.
+  parts.push(
+    'It must export exactly these symbols, with exactly these signatures:\n'
+    + task.exportedSymbols.map((s) => `- ${s.signature}`).join('\n'),
+  );
   if (task.constraints.length > 0) {
     parts.push(`Constraints:\n${task.constraints.map((c) => `- ${c}`).join('\n')}`);
   }

nodes.label: n005
nodes.author: 0b3c69814f295bb73e4affb25fd2d88a5765e598b047809149edb8954041e584
nodes.hypothesis: The worked example and the full signatures are redundant, because the model already infers the reply shape from the symbol names alone. Removing them keeps the score and saves input tokens.
nodes.statusReason: 2 verifications from distinct keys, every one at or below -1000bp. Best delta -7000bp. This is a measured regression. The change makes the harness worse. The ledger is a local log, so one person can hold every key. Distinct keys are not proof of distinct people. Run `petri topic create` to publish.

proposal.hypothesis: The worked example and the full signatures are redundant, because the model already infers the reply shape from the symbol names alone. Removing them keeps the score and saves input tokens.
proposal.falsifiedIf: The candidate median score falls below the parent median by 1000 basis points or more.
proposal.reasoning: The example costs input tokens on every task. If the model infers the shape from the names, the shorter prompt is strictly better.
proposal.whyNotUntested: The prompt area is the only area a single measured node has moved so far, so its limit is the one fact this tree can test.
